tasks.subject: [agent-home-desk] [P1] Read every agent identity from its registered home
tasks.description: Spec §3.1-§3.3, invariants I1 and I2. Closes DOR-2355's literal ask on its own. Add `agent-home.ts` with the branded `AgentHome` and `resolveAgentHome` (exact, linked worktree of a home repo by the `.git` file and commondir with no git process, managed workspace by owner.ref), fold `resolveIdentityAnchor` into it (keep the room-worktree owner source for now; T4 removes it), and switch every site in §3.2 rows 1-12 to read from the home. Add `MessageOpts.forAgent` (row 12) and send it from task and relay dispatch. Mesh refuses to register under `<dorkHome>/rooms/`. Changelog fragment: agents in a git worktree of their own repo keep their name, persona, memory and Claude account. Also forward `forAgent` by name through message-dispatcher.ts (the turn Pick whitelist ~:955-970 and the launch spread ~:1236-1250), with a queued-path test. Resolver hardening per §3.1: require git's gitdir backlink, missing commondir answers none, source-2 memo keyed on the .git and gitdir file contents.
validation: For each §3.2 row, a test with a home-repo worktree whose committed .dork/ differs from the home shows the home's values (context text, launch options, account root, runtime choice, relay label, get_agent, GET /agents/current).
The same worktree with .dork/ deleted still resolves to the agent.

Resolver unit cases in §11 pass, including bare repo, rooms common dir (no registry lookup), non-matching subfolder, managed owned by the agent with a foreign source, forAgent mismatch, and memo invalidation on unregister.
Registering a candidate under <dorkHome>/rooms is refused `inside-room-files`; a linked worktree of a registered home is refused `duplicate-id` (named test).
buildAgentContextAppend, the context-builder agent block, and the launch-resolver manifest read accept AgentHome only (a string cwd fails typecheck).
pnpm --filter @dorkos/server typecheck, lint and the touched vitest files pass.

Resolver hardening tests (§11): hand-written .git pointer without backlink → none; submodule .git (no commondir) → none; worktree removed and re-added at the same path by another repo → new owner.

tasks.subject: [agent-home-desk] [P1] Grant folders per turn on every runtime, gated by conformance

tasks.description: Spec §4. Add `DirectoryGrant` and `MessageOpts.additionalDirectories` plus `@dorkos/shared/directory-grants` validation. Forward `additionalDirectories` by name through message-dispatcher.ts (whitelist + launch spread) with a queued-path test. claude-code: settings.permissions.additionalDirectories + `//` deny rules for read grants, merged into the existing settings object via a new directory-grants.ts; strip CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD from the turn env; add the fingerprint pin. codex: write grants into ThreadOptions.additionalDirectories. opencode: per-session PermissionRuleset via session.update when the set changes (ask-handler fallback if needed). test-mode declares an unproven reason. Add the §4.6 conformance case and wire it for all three runtimes. Nothing calls it yet, so no user-visible change; ship with skip-changelog only if no fragment is warranted (internal).

The --add-dir fallback is taken only if (a1) or (a2) fails, and the spec is amended when it is.
Conformance case passes on claude-code (warm session asserted), codex and opencode mocked legs; test-mode declares its reason; the pairing test fails a runtime that declares neither.
Turn 2 of the conformance case hands C and neither A nor B on every runtime.
Fingerprint: changed set relaunches, reordered set does not.

tasks.subject: [agent-home-desk] [P1] Build the move of room transcripts from worktree folders to the agent's home folder
tasks.description: Spec §8.1. Build migrate-room-transcripts.ts: marker-guarded, idempotent move of claude-code room transcripts from projects/<slug(worktree)>/ to projects/<slug(home)>/ across every Claude config dir DorkOS launches with, recording the frozen worktree list in the marker. On a colliding destination the source is renamed <id>.jsonl.conflict (so the JSONL frontier never sees two transcripts for one id) and both paths are logged and recorded for the operator. Measure codex and opencode listing and resume across a desk change and write the result into §8.1. This task does NOT wire the migration into startup and does not touch extraDirs: moving transcripts while room turns still run in worktrees would break their resume, so T4 wires both in the same PR that moves the desk. The module is unused between this PR and T4 on purpose (a staged programme; T4 is blocked on it). No changelog fragment.
validation: Fixture test: two worktree slugs (registered + unregistered agent) and a colliding destination → moved / skipped / source renamed .jsonl.conflict and named in log and marker; the frontier indexes exactly one transcript for that id; marker written with the frozen list; second run no-op.
Every Claude config dir (default + account pins) is visited (test with two dirs).
Live check recorded in the PR: a claude-code room session moved by the module (run by hand against a copy) resumes with its history when launched with cwd = the home.
codex and opencode measurement recorded in §8.1, stating for each whether extraDirs must keep a frozen list.
filesOwned: apps/server/src/services/runtimes/claude-code/migrate-room-transcripts.ts (new; not sessions/, which is at the 25-file dir-size cap) + its test

tasks.subject: [agent-home-desk] [P2] Room turns run in the agent's own folder with the room's files granted
tasks.activeForm: Moving room turns back to the agent's home
tasks.description: Spec §5 and §3.4. The agent-facing truth flips atomically here: resolveRoomTurnPlace (cwd = home, three grants), dispatcher/runner/app-resume carry grants and forAgent, the rewritten context-block files section, the rewritten working-in-room-repos skill (OPERATING_SKILLS_VERSION bump), canvas resolveTree by source path, the desk guard (DOR-2356) at room/relay/task dispatch, the §5.8 removal list, §5.9 legacy plumbing retirement, and the §8.1 wiring: run the T3 migration at startup before the room dispatcher starts, and switch extraDirs to the frozen list (or delete it) per the T3 measurement. Adds the eval case (room turn edits a room file by absolute path) to the policed tier array. Also: add DispatchMessageOpts.prepareLaunch (awaited by message-dispatcher.ts where an immediate or dequeued turn is about to call runtime.sendMessage, forwarded by name in the whitelist and launch spread) and message-dispatcher isTurnInFlight(sessionId); T4 uses it for §5.9 legacy clean-up, T5 for the refresh. The changelog fragment also says: an agent set to use no folder of its own can no longer run in another agent's folder (in a DorkOS dev checkout, where the default folder is the dorkos agent's home, such tasks now stop with a message saying to set a default folder).

tasks.subject: [agent-home-desk] [P3] Bring an agent's copy of the room's files up to date at turn start
tasks.activeForm: Refreshing room worktrees at turn start
tasks.description: Spec §6. room-worktree-refresh.ts run from the room turn's prepareLaunch (added in T4), never at placement: capture mainTip first; skip with held:busy if any session bound to the (room, agent) has a turn in flight; hold on branch, changes, ahead, and any ignored or untracked file at a path the fast-forward would write; then ff-only to the captured tip. The MainMoved heads-up uses --first-parent and names commits from their room entries (merge or fileChange), never git authors; subjects and paths render inside the untrusted fence. §6.3 context lines; EditBaselineStore.forget. Changelog fragment: agents start each room turn on the latest files when they have nothing in progress, and are told what changed when they do.
validation: Every §11 Refresh and Heads-up unit test passes, each held reason red-before/green-after.
Ignored-file test: notes.log ignored in the worktree, then committed on main → held: changes and notes.log bytes unchanged; the same for an untracked file at a parent-folder path.

Folder-becomes-file test: ignored build/keep.txt under a build/ rule; main commits a tracked file `build` and drops the rule → held: changes, build/keep.txt still exists (step 6 checks equal, inside and parent in both directions).

Busy test with two bound sessions: while a turn runs on a second session bound to the same (room, agent) (e.g. app-resumed), a room turn launched on the first answers held: busy with zero git calls, and refreshes after the second settles.

Lossy-inFlight test: the second session's turn launched with its queue budget exhausted (runtime lock held, no inFlight entry) still yields held: busy — isTurnInFlight reads inFlight OR the runtime lock/streaming state.
Launch-not-placement test: a turn placed while main is at A and launched after main moved to B lands on B.
main advancing after mainTip is captured: worktree lands exactly on the captured tip.
--first-parent test: merging a 12-commit agent branch lists one commit; people named from room entries (two signed-in people told apart); a hand commit is 'other'.
Integration test (§11 Integration, second half) passes.
contributing/room-repos.md no longer says the server never mutates a worktree; it describes the one exception.
